core_message: If you keep lowering your price, the problem may not be your pricing strategy. You may be protecting yourself from rejection.
problem: An experienced expert knows their work is valuable but feels uncomfortable naming a higher price and unconsciously reduces the price to make rejection feel less threatening.
reframe: Undercharging is not always modesty or market strategy. Sometimes it is a way to reduce the emotional risk of hearing no.
key_points: You know your expertise is valuable.
You prepare to name your price and feel tension or hesitation.
You lower the price before the client even objects.
The lower price can temporarily reduce fear of rejection.
The deeper work is learning to tolerate the emotional discomfort of being fully visible and appropriately priced.
hook: You might not be undercharging because you're modest.
audience_takeaway: Before changing your pricing strategy, notice what emotion appears when you imagine saying your real price.
